title.en: Tests of adequacy of index numbers

heading.en: Is the index a good one?

hook.en: If prices doubled from 2015 to 2025, then going back from 2025 to 2015 they must halve. Does every formula agree? Tests of adequacy check this.
hook.kn: 2015 ರಿಂದ 2025 ಕ್ಕೆ ಬೆಲೆ ದ್ವಿಗುಣವಾದರೆ, ಹಿಂತಿರುಗಿದಾಗ ಅರ್ಧವಾಗಬೇಕು. ಎಲ್ಲ ಸೂತ್ರಗಳೂ ಇದನ್ನು ಒಪ್ಪುತ್ತವೆಯೇ? ಸಮರ್ಪಕತಾ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗಳು ಇದನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: State the unit, time reversal and factor reversal tests
Verify the tests for given data
Explain why Fisher's index is ideal

narration.en: If prices doubled from 2015 to 2025, then going back from 2025 to 2015 they must halve. Does every formula agree? Tests of adequacy check this.
narration.kn: 2015 ರಿಂದ 2025 ಕ್ಕೆ ಬೆಲೆ ದ್ವಿಗುಣವಾದರೆ, ಹಿಂತಿರುಗಿದಾಗ ಅರ್ಧವಾಗಬೇಕು. ಎಲ್ಲ ಸೂತ್ರಗಳೂ ಇದನ್ನು ಒಪ್ಪುತ್ತವೆಯೇ? ಸಮರ್ಪಕತಾ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗಳು ಇದನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Unit test: the index should not depend on the units in which prices are quoted (all except the simple aggregative index pass). Time reversal test: $P_{01} \times P_{10} = 1$ (indices as ratios). Factor reversal test: $P_{01} \times Q_{01} = V_{01} = \frac{\sum p_1 q_1}{\sum p_0 q_0}$. Fisher's index satisfies both reversal tests, so it is called the ideal index number. Laspeyres' and Paasche's satisfy neither; Marshall–Edgeworth and Kelly satisfy the time reversal test only.

narration.en: The time reversal test asks that P zero one times P one zero equals one. The factor reversal test asks that the price index times the quantity index equals the value index. Fisher's index passes both, so it is ideal.
narration.kn: ಸಮಯ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಯ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ: P₀₁ × P₁₀ = 1. ಅಂಶ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಯ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ: ಬೆಲೆ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ × ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ = ಮೌಲ್ಯ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ. ಫಿಶರ್ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ ಎರಡನ್ನೂ ಪೂರೈಸುವುದರಿಂದ ಅದು ಆದರ್ಶ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ.

blocks.formula: P_{01} \times P_{10} = 1, \qquad P_{01} \times Q_{01} = \frac{\sum p_1 q_1}{\sum p_0 q_0}

narration.en: The board writes the two reversal tests, shows why Fisher's index passes, and ends with a score card.

say.en: Time reversal: swap the years. Product of the two indices must be one.
For Fisher, the base and current terms cancel inside the root.

draw.tex: \sqrt{\frac{\sum p_1q_0}{\sum p_0q_0}\frac{\sum p_1q_1}{\sum p_0q_1}\cdot\frac{\sum p_0q_1}{\sum p_1q_1}\frac{\sum p_0q_0}{\sum p_1q_0}} = 1

say.en: Factor reversal: swap p and q to get the quantity index; the product must be the value index.
Score card: only Fisher passes all three tests.

narration.en: Sort each index number by the reversal tests it satisfies.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕವನ್ನು ಅದು ತೃಪ್ತಿಪಡಿಸುವ ಹಿಮ್ಮುಖ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗಳ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ.

explanation.en: Only Fisher's ideal index satisfies both the time reversal and the factor reversal tests. Marshall–Edgeworth, Kelly's, the simple aggregative index and the simple GM of relatives satisfy the time reversal test only. Laspeyres', Paasche's, Dorbish–Bowley and the simple AM of relatives satisfy neither.

caption.en: Change this year's quantity of rice. Laspeyres' P₀₁ × P₁₀ moves away from 1; Fisher's stays exactly 1 and also passes the factor reversal test.

tryThis.en: Is there any rice quantity for which Laspeyres' passes the time reversal test?
Compare the last two readouts for several settings.

narration.en: Test the formulas numerically: the products show which index passes each reversal test.

problem.en: For the four-item data (p₀ = [40, 80, 20, 100], q₀ = [10, 5, 20, 4], p₁ = [60, 100, 30, 120], q₁ = [12, 6, 18, 5]), show that Fisher's index satisfies the factor reversal test.

steps.en: P₀₁ × Q₀₁ = 1.5375 = 2,460/1,600 = V₀₁. Hence FRT is satisfied.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. For the four-item data (p₀ = [40, 80, 20, 100], q₀ = [10, 5, 20, 4], p₁ = [60, 100, 30, 120], q₁ = [12, 6, 18, 5]), show that Fisher's index satisfies the factor reversal test.

body.en: Remember: Fisher passes the time reversal and factor reversal tests. Laspeyres' and Paasche's pass neither reversal test.
